meanings.definition: Used to join two words, phrases or ideas together.

examples.text: I like apples and oranges very much.
My sister and I walk to school every day.

meanings.definition: Used to show that one thing happens after another.

examples.text: She opened the door and walked into the room.
He finished his dinner and went to bed.

meanings.definition: Used to show that the second thing happens because of the first.

examples.text: Work hard and you will pass the test.
Eat less sugar and you will feel better.

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to or is part of something else.

examples.text: What is the name of your dog?
The end of the film was very sad.

meanings.definition: Used after a word for an amount or a container.

examples.text: Can I have a cup of tea, please?
She bought a bottle of water at the shop.

meanings.definition: Used to say what a picture, map or story shows.

examples.text: She showed me a picture of her new house.
I have a map of the city in my bag.

meanings.definition: Used to show the place where someone or something goes.

examples.text: We walk to school every morning.
Next summer I want to visit Paris.

meanings.definition: Used to show who gets or receives something.

examples.text: She gave the book to her brother.
Please send this letter to my mother.

meanings.definition: Used to show the end of a period of time or a range.

examples.text: The shop is open from nine to five.
I work from Monday to Friday every week.

meanings.definition: Into or inside a place, such as a room or a building.

examples.text: It is raining, so please come in quickly.
I knocked on the door, and she let me in.

meanings.definition: Used to say that something is inside a place or thing.

examples.text: The keys are in my bag by the door.
My parents live in a small town near the sea.

meanings.definition: Used with months, years, seasons and parts of the day.

examples.text: My birthday is in June, near the summer holidays.
I always drink coffee in the morning.

meanings.definition: Used to say how long before something will happen.

examples.text: The train will leave in ten minutes.
I will call you back in an hour.

meanings.definition: Used for a thing or animal that was already talked about.

examples.text: I lost my phone, and I can't find it.
This cake is great. Did you make it yourself?

meanings.definition: Used as the subject when talking about the weather, the time or distance.

examples.text: It is very cold and windy today.
It is three o'clock, so we must go now.

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to a thing or an animal.

examples.text: The dog is playing with its ball.
The tree lost all its leaves in autumn.

meanings.definition: Used for the person or people someone is speaking to.

examples.text: Are you ready to go to the park?
I will see you at school tomorrow.

meanings.definition: Used for people in general, not one special person.

examples.text: You can buy stamps at the post office.
You should always wash fruit before eating it.

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to the person someone is speaking to.

examples.text: Is this your bag on the chair?
What is your favourite colour, red or blue?

meanings.definition: Used for a man, boy or male animal already talked about.

examples.text: My brother is tall, and he plays basketball.
Where is Tom? He is in the garden.

meanings.definition: Used after a verb or preposition for a man or boy.

examples.text: I saw Peter yesterday and talked to him.
This is my uncle. Do you know him?

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to a man or boy.

examples.text: Tom lost his keys at the station.
My father drives his car to work every day.

meanings.definition: Used, mostly in formal writing, to give the reason for something.

examples.text: She stayed at home, for she felt very ill.
We had to stop, for it was getting dark.

meanings.definition: Used to say who will get or use something.

examples.text: I bought these flowers for my mother.
There is a message for you on the table.

meanings.definition: Used to say how long something lasts.

examples.text: We lived in Paris for three years.
She slept for ten hours last night.

meanings.definition: Used to say why someone goes somewhere or what they want.

examples.text: Let's go out for dinner tonight.
We stopped at a cafe for a coffee.

meanings.definition: Used for two or more people or things already talked about.

examples.text: My friends are late because they missed the bus.
I like these shoes, but they are too small.

meanings.definition: Used after a verb or preposition for two or more people or things.

examples.text: I called my parents and told them the news.
Where are my keys? I can't find them.

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to two or more people or things.

examples.text: The children are playing in their room.
My neighbours sold their car last week.

meanings.definition: Used to make a word, phrase or sentence negative.

examples.text: I am not hungry right now, thank you.
This coffee is not hot enough.

meanings.definition: Used after verbs like hope or think to give a short negative answer.

examples.text: Is it going to rain today? I hope not.
Will the shop be open on Sunday? Probably not.

meanings.definition: Used to mean "so" or "very", often in negative sentences.

examples.text: The film was not that good, to be honest.
I didn't know the test was that hard.

meanings.definition: Used after verbs like say, think or know to begin the next part of a sentence.

examples.text: He said that he was tired and hungry.
My mum knows that I like chocolate cake.

meanings.definition: Used after "so" or "such" to show a result.

examples.text: It was so hot that we stayed inside all day.
He was so tired that he fell asleep early.

meanings.definition: Used for a person or thing that is not near the speaker.

examples.text: What is that on the kitchen floor?
Is that your bike outside the house?

meanings.definition: Used for two or more people or things that are not near the speaker.

examples.text: Those are my grandparents in the photo.
Are those your books on the table?

meanings.definition: Used to begin a part of a sentence that tells you more about a noun.

examples.text: This is the book that I told you about.
The man that lives next door is a doctor.

meanings.definition: Used by a speaker for themselves and one or more other people.

examples.text: My sister and I are happy because we won.
We are going to the beach tomorrow.

meanings.definition: Used after a verb or preposition for the speaker and other people.

examples.text: Can you help us with these heavy bags?
The teacher gave us a lot of homework today.

meanings.definition: Used to show that something belongs to the speaker and other people.

examples.text: Our house has a big garden at the back.
Please come to our party on Saturday night.

meanings.definition: Working or being used, like a light or a machine.

examples.text: Please turn the lights on, it's dark in here.
Is the TV still on in the living room?

meanings.definition: Used to show that an action continues or moves forward.

examples.text: Please go on, I'm listening to your story.
We walked on until we reached the river.

meanings.definition: Touching the top of a surface, like a table or a floor.

examples.text: Your phone is on the kitchen table.
There is a picture on the wall above the bed.

meanings.definition: Used before days of the week and dates.

examples.text: We have a test on Monday morning.
My birthday is on the fifth of May.

meanings.definition: Used to say what something is shown or heard through, like TV or the phone.

examples.text: I watched a good film on TV last night.
She is talking to her friend on the phone.

meanings.definition: Used to show that people or things are together.

examples.text: I live with my parents and my sister.
Do you want to come with us to the cinema?

meanings.definition: Used to say what tool or thing is used to do something.

examples.text: She cut the bread with a sharp knife.
Please write your name with a pen.

meanings.definition: Used to say that someone or something has a certain thing.

examples.text: She is the girl with long red hair.
I want a room with a view of the sea.

meanings.definition: A word for a person or thing that is near you or that you are showing.

examples.text: Is this your bag, or is it mine?
These are my new shoes. Do you like them?

meanings.definition: A word you use when you tell people the name of a person or say who is speaking.

examples.text: Mum, this is my friend Tom from school.
Hello, this is Anna. Can I speak to Ben?

meanings.definition: A word for something that is happening now or that you have just talked about.

examples.text: The train is late again. This happens every day.
Listen to this: we won a free holiday!

meanings.definition: A word the speaker or writer uses to talk about themselves as the subject of a sentence.

examples.text: I live in a small house near the river.
My sister is tall, but I am short.

meanings.definition: The word the speaker uses for themselves after a verb or after words like to, with and for.

examples.text: Can you help me with my homework, please?
My friends sent me a nice card today.

meanings.definition: Words that show something belongs to the person who is speaking.

examples.text: This is my brother, and he is ten.
That red bike is not yours. It is mine.

meanings.definition: A word that shows two things happen at the same time.

examples.text: She smiled as she opened the door.
The phone rang just as I was leaving the house.

meanings.definition: A word that gives the reason for something.

examples.text: We stayed at home as it was raining all day.
As I was tired, I went to bed early.

meanings.definition: A word that shows something happens in the way that someone says or does.

examples.text: Please do it as I showed you yesterday.
As you know, the shop is closed on Sundays.

meanings.definition: A word that shows the job, role or use that a person or thing has.

examples.text: My mother works as a teacher in a big school.
We used an old box as a table.

meanings.definition: Used in the pattern "as big as" to say two people or things are the same in some way.

examples.text: My brother is now as tall as my father.
Come home as soon as you can, please.

meanings.definition: A word that talks about a time in someone's life, such as when they were young.

examples.text: As a child, I lived on a farm.
She was very shy as a young girl.

meanings.definition: A word that shows where someone or something is.

examples.text: I will meet you at the bus station.
The children are at school until three o'clock.

meanings.definition: A word that shows the exact time when something happens.

examples.text: The film starts at seven o'clock tonight.
We usually eat lunch at one in the afternoon.

meanings.definition: A word that shows who or what you look, point or smile toward.

examples.text: Look at that big dog in the garden!
The baby smiled at her mother.

meanings.definition: A word for a woman, girl or female animal already talked about, as the subject of a sentence.

examples.text: My sister is a doctor. She works in a hospital.
Where is Maria? Is she still at work?

meanings.definition: The word for a woman or girl after a verb or after words like to, with and for.

examples.text: I saw Lucy yesterday and gave her the book.
My grandmother lives alone, so we visit her often.

meanings.definition: Words that show something belongs to a woman or girl.

examples.text: Anna lost her phone on the train.
That is not my coat. I think it is hers.

meanings.definition: A word that joins two ideas when the second one is different or surprising.

examples.text: The hotel was small but very clean.
I like tea, but my husband likes coffee.

meanings.definition: A word used before saying sorry or giving a reason why you cannot do something.

examples.text: I'm sorry, but I can't come to your party.
Excuse me, but is this seat free?

meanings.definition: A word that means apart from or not including someone or something.

examples.text: Everyone but Sam came to the meeting.
He eats nothing but bread and cheese.

meanings.definition: A word that shows the place where someone or something starts or comes from.

examples.text: I'm from Spain, but I live in London now.
She walked home from the station in the rain.

meanings.definition: A word that shows who sent or gave something.

examples.text: I got a long letter from my aunt today.
These flowers are a present from my children.

meanings.definition: A word that shows when something starts, often used with to or until.

examples.text: The shop is open from nine to five.
I work from Monday to Friday every week.

meanings.definition: A word that shows how you travel or how something is done.

examples.text: We went to Paris by train last summer.
You can pay by card in this shop.

meanings.definition: A word that shows who wrote, made or did something.

examples.text: This book was written by a famous teacher.
The window was broken by a football.

meanings.definition: A word that shows the latest time when something must happen.

examples.text: Please send me your homework by Friday.
The train will arrive by six o'clock.

meanings.definition: The strong wish and mental strength to decide something and make it happen.

examples.text: She had the will to keep training after her injury.
He lost the will to fight and finally gave up.

meanings.definition: A legal document saying who should get a person's money and property after they die.

examples.text: In his will, my grandfather left the house to my mother.
Older people are advised to write a will with a lawyer.

meanings.definition: A word that joins two or more possibilities when only one is chosen.

examples.text: Would you like tea or coffee with your cake?
We can go by bus or walk to the park.

meanings.definition: A word that shows what will happen if someone does not do something.

examples.text: Hurry up, or we will miss the train.
Wear a coat, or you will get cold outside.

meanings.definition: The right or chance to give your opinion and help decide something.

examples.text: Workers want more say in how the company is run.
The children had no say in where the family moved.

meanings.definition: To speak words to someone.

examples.text: She said goodbye and closed the door.
How do you say "thank you" in Japanese?

meanings.definition: To tell people what you think, or what is true or reported.

examples.text: My doctor says I should eat more fruit.
People say this is the best pizza in town.

meanings.definition: To give information in writing, or show it with numbers or pictures.

examples.text: The sign says the museum is closed on Mondays.
What time does your watch say?

meanings.definition: A time when you try to do something, often for the first time.

examples.text: I've never played this game, but I'll have a go.
She passed her driving test on the first go.

meanings.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.

examples.text: We go to the beach every summer.
Last night I went to bed at ten o'clock.

meanings.definition: To happen or develop in a good or bad way.

examples.text: How did your exam go this morning?
The party went very well, and everyone was happy.

meanings.definition: To change and become different, often in a bad way.

examples.text: The milk has gone bad, so don't drink it.
His face went red when she smiled at him.

meanings.definition: A word that makes an adjective or adverb stronger.

examples.text: The film was so funny that we laughed all night.
Thank you so much for your help today.

meanings.definition: A word used instead of repeating an idea that was just said.

examples.text: "Is the shop open now?" "I think so."
"Will it rain tomorrow?" "I hope not, but maybe so."

meanings.definition: A word used to say that the same is true for another person or thing.

examples.text: "I'm really hungry." "So am I. Let's eat."
My sister plays the piano, and so does my brother.

meanings.definition: A word that introduces the result of something.

examples.text: It was raining, so we stayed at home.
I was very tired, so I went to bed early.

meanings.definition: A word that shows the purpose of an action, often with that.

examples.text: Speak louder so that everyone can hear you.
I left early so I wouldn't miss the bus.

meanings.definition: A word that means completely or totally.

examples.text: After the party, she was all alone in the house.
The children came home all wet from the rain.

meanings.definition: A word that means every person or thing in a group.

examples.text: I invited ten friends, and all of them came.
We all like pizza, so let's order two.

meanings.definition: A word that means the whole amount, or the only thing.

examples.text: Is that all you want for dinner?
All I need now is a hot shower.

meanings.definition: Used to say that one thing happens only when another thing happens.

examples.text: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
You can have some cake if you finish your dinner.

meanings.definition: Used to ask or talk about whether something is true.

examples.text: I don't know if she is at home now.
Can you ask him if he wants a cup of tea?

meanings.definition: A single person or thing from a group.

examples.text: One of my friends lives in a big city.
She is one of the best students in our class.

meanings.definition: Used so that you do not have to repeat a noun.

examples.text: I don't like this shirt. Can I see that one?
My shoes are very old, so I need new ones.

meanings.definition: A formal way of talking about any person or people in general.

examples.text: One should always be polite to other people.
One can learn a lot from making mistakes.

meanings.definition: A little more or a little less than a number or amount.

examples.text: The trip takes about two hours by train.
There were about fifty people at the party.

meanings.definition: In many different places, or moving in no special direction.

examples.text: The children were running about in the garden all afternoon.
Your clothes are lying about all over the floor.

meanings.definition: Used to say what something is connected with or what it tells you.

examples.text: This book is about a young girl and her dog.
We talked about our plans for the weekend.

meanings.definition: Used with "how" or "what" to suggest something or ask an opinion.

examples.text: How about going to the cinema tonight?
I'm hungry. What about pizza for dinner?

meanings.definition: A closed metal container for food or drink, or the amount it holds.

examples.text: I opened a can of tomatoes for the soup.
He drank two cans of cola after the game.

meanings.definition: Used to ask about one or more things from a small group.

examples.text: Which is your bag, the red one or the blue one?
Which of these two cakes do you like best?

meanings.definition: Used to add information about the thing or animal you have just mentioned.

examples.text: This is the house which my grandfather built.
I lost the watch which my father gave me.

meanings.definition: Used after a comma to say something about the whole of the earlier idea.

examples.text: He missed the bus, which made him late for work.
She passed all her exams, which surprised everyone.

meanings.definition: In, at or to a place that is not here.

examples.text: Put the box over there, next to the door.
I went to Paris last year and loved it there.

meanings.definition: To have facts or information about something in your mind.

examples.text: Do you know where the train station is?
I knew the answer, but I forgot it.

meanings.definition: To have met a person before, or to be familiar with a place.

examples.text: I have known Tom since we were children.
Do you know this part of the city well?

meanings.definition: To have learned how to do something.

examples.text: She knows how to cook really good pasta.
My little brother doesn't know how to swim yet.

meanings.definition: Used before adjectives and adverbs to compare two things.

examples.text: This book is more interesting than the film.
Please speak more slowly so I can understand you.

meanings.definition: A greater number of times or to a greater amount than before.

examples.text: I should exercise more and eat less sugar.
She travels more now that her children have grown up.

meanings.definition: A larger or extra amount or number of something.

examples.text: Would you like some more? There is plenty of soup.
We need more of these chairs for the party.

meanings.definition: Used with "than" to say a number is higher.

examples.text: More than fifty people came to the meeting.
This bag costs more than I wanted to pay.

meanings.definition: To receive, buy or be given something.

examples.text: I got a new phone for my birthday.
Where did you get that nice jacket?

meanings.definition: To start to be in a new state.

examples.text: It gets dark very early in the winter.
Please don't get angry, it was only a joke.

meanings.definition: To arrive at a place.

examples.text: What time did you get home last night?
We got to the station just before the train left.

meanings.definition: Used to ask which person or people.

examples.text: Who is that man next to your sister?
Who did you see at the party last night?

meanings.definition: Used to add information about the person you have just mentioned.

examples.text: The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
I have a friend who speaks four languages.

meanings.definition: Used to ask which person something belongs to.

examples.text: Whose bag is this on the kitchen table?
Whose car is parked in front of our house?

meanings.definition: In the same way that someone does or something happens.

examples.text: Nobody makes soup like my grandmother did.
Do the exercise like I showed you yesterday.

meanings.definition: Used to say how something seems or appears.

examples.text: It looks like it is going to rain soon.
He talks like he knows everything about cars.

meanings.definition: Almost the same as someone or something else.

examples.text: She looks like her mother when she smiles.
This fruit tastes a bit like a sweet apple.

meanings.definition: Used in questions to ask what a person or thing is really like.

examples.text: What is your new teacher like?
What was the weather like on your holiday?

meanings.definition: Used to give examples of the things you mean.

examples.text: I enjoy sports like tennis and swimming.
Fruits like apples and oranges are good for you.

meanings.definition: To enjoy something or think that someone or something is nice.

examples.text: I like playing football with my friends.
My sister really likes her new school.

meanings.definition: Used with "would" to say politely what you want.

examples.text: I would like a cup of tea, please.
Would you like to come to my party?

meanings.definition: Used to ask at what time something happens.

examples.text: When is your birthday this year?
When did you arrive in London?

meanings.definition: Used after a time word to add information about that time.

examples.text: I remember the day when we first met.
Summer is the season when most people go on holiday.

meanings.definition: Used to say the time at which something happens.

examples.text: I was very happy when I heard the news.
Please call me when you get home.

meanings.definition: Used to show surprise that something happens although something else is true.

examples.text: Why buy a new bike when you can fix the old one?
He said he was busy when he was just watching TV.

meanings.definition: To have an opinion or believe that something is true.

examples.text: I think this film is really good.
Do you think it will rain tomorrow?

meanings.definition: To use your mind to consider something or solve a problem.

examples.text: Think carefully before you answer the question.
I was thinking about my holiday all day.

meanings.definition: To consider doing something in the future.

examples.text: We're thinking of moving to a bigger house.
She is thinking about changing her job next year.

meanings.definition: The name of the company that produced a product.

examples.text: What make is your new car?
This make of phone is very popular with students.

meanings.definition: To produce something by putting parts together or by cooking.

examples.text: My mother made a big cake for my birthday.
This company makes toys for small children.

meanings.definition: To cause someone or something to be or do something.

examples.text: That funny film always makes me laugh.
The teacher made us do the work again.

meanings.definition: To earn money from work or business.

examples.text: She makes a lot of money at her new job.
How much money does a nurse make in a month?

meanings.definition: The hour and minutes shown on a clock or watch.

examples.text: Excuse me, what time is it? I don't have a watch.
What time does the film start tonight?

meanings.definition: One occasion when something happens.

examples.text: I have been to London three times with my family.
The first time I saw the sea, I was five.

meanings.definition: The minutes, hours or days that you have to do something.

examples.text: Sorry, I don't have time to cook dinner tonight.
We have a lot of time before the train leaves.

meanings.definition: To measure how long something takes or how fast someone does it.

examples.text: The coach timed each runner over one hundred metres.
I always time myself when I do a practice exam.

meanings.definition: To choose or plan the moment when something happens.

examples.text: They timed their holiday to miss the busy summer months.
Good timing is important when you tell a joke.

meanings.definition: To notice someone or something using your eyes.

examples.text: I can see the mountains from my bedroom window.
Did you see that big bird on the roof?

meanings.definition: To understand an idea or the reason for something.

examples.text: Oh, I see what you mean now. Thanks for explaining.
Do you see why this answer is wrong?

meanings.definition: To meet or visit someone, for example a friend or a doctor.

examples.text: We see our grandparents every Sunday afternoon.
I'm seeing the doctor tomorrow morning about my back.

meanings.definition: A word used to ask about a thing, an action or information.

examples.text: What is your favourite food?
What did you buy at the market this morning?

meanings.definition: A word that means the thing or things that.

examples.text: I didn't understand what the teacher said in class.
Show me what you have in your bag, please.

meanings.definition: Towards a higher place or position.

examples.text: The balloon flew up into the sky and was gone.
He looked up and saw a plane above the house.

meanings.definition: To a bigger amount, a higher level or a louder sound.

examples.text: Can you turn the music up? I can't hear it.
Food prices have gone up a lot this year.

meanings.definition: From a lower place to a higher place on something.

examples.text: We walked up the hill to the old church.
The boy ran up the stairs to his room.

meanings.definition: Along a road or street, a little further on.

examples.text: There is a small café just up the road from my house.
Go up this street and turn left at the bank.

meanings.definition: An amount or number of something, when the exact amount is not said.

examples.text: I made fresh coffee. Would you like some?
These apples are really nice. Can I have some?

meanings.definition: A part of a group of people or things, but not all of them.

examples.text: Some of my friends live in the city centre.
Some of the students were late for class today.

meanings.definition: The remaining person or thing, or the remaining people or things in a group.

examples.text: Tom is here, but where are the others?
I found one shoe, but I can't find the other.

meanings.definition: Different people or things from the ones already talked about.

examples.text: Some people like tea, and others prefer coffee.
Try to be kind and help others when you can.

meanings.definition: Away from your home or the place where you work.

examples.text: Sorry, my mum is out at the moment. Call again later.
We went out for dinner on Friday night.

meanings.definition: Moving from inside a place or container to the outside.

examples.text: She opened the door and walked out into the garden.
Please take the milk out of the fridge.

meanings.definition: Pleasant, or of a high quality.

examples.text: This is a really good book. You should read it.
We had good weather on our holiday by the sea.

meanings.definition: Able to do something with skill.

examples.text: My sister is very good at maths and science.
He is a good cook and makes great pasta.

meanings.definition: Kind and honest, or behaving in the right way.

examples.text: She is a good person who always helps her neighbours.
The children were very good on the long car trip.

meanings.definition: Something that helps a person or makes their life better.

examples.text: Eat your vegetables. It's for your own good.
A week by the sea will do you a lot of good.

meanings.definition: Behaviour or forces that are right and honest, the opposite of evil.

examples.text: Many old stories are about the fight between good and evil.
Children slowly learn the difference between good and bad.

meanings.definition: Men, women and children; more than one person.

examples.text: There were a lot of people at the concert last night.
How many people live in your house?

meanings.definition: All the persons who belong to one nation, culture or group.

examples.text: Many different peoples have lived in this region over the centuries.
The president promised to listen to the people of the country.

meanings.definition: A period of twelve months, or 365 days.

examples.text: She has lived in Paris for three years.
My little brother is six years old.

meanings.definition: The part of a year when a school, college or business is working.

examples.text: The new school year starts in September.
My brother is in his last year at university.

meanings.definition: One recording of a scene in a film, done without stopping.

examples.text: The actor finally got the scene right on the third take.
We needed ten takes because the dog kept running away.

meanings.definition: To get hold of something with your hands, or to accept or choose it.

examples.text: She took a book from the shelf and started reading.
You can take an apple from the bowl if you're hungry.

meanings.definition: To carry something or go with someone from one place to another.

examples.text: I take my son to school every morning.
Don't forget to take an umbrella with you today.

You're the very person I wanted to talk to!

She uses her bike to get to school.

examples.text: Big cars use a lot of gas.
We used all the milk this morning.

examples.text: My brother is taller than I am.

examples.text: I would rather walk than wait for the bus.

My sister is two years older than me.

examples.text: More than fifty people came to the party.
The shop is less than a minute from here.

This room is for teachers only.

Children must learn the difference between needs and wants.

meanings.definition: The person or thing farther away from the speaker, which you point to or show.

examples.text: Look at that big dog over there!
What is that on the top of the tree?

meanings.definition: The idea or fact someone has just said or done.

examples.text: You can come with us? That is great news!
He lost his phone again, and that made him angry.

meanings.definition: Used after a noun to begin the part of a sentence that tells you more about it.

examples.text: This is the book that I read last summer.
The man that lives next door is a doctor.

meanings.definition: The speaker and one or more other people, but not the person being spoken to.

examples.text: My brother and I play football, and we often win.
We are from Japan. Where are you from?

meanings.definition: The speaker and the person being spoken to, together.

examples.text: Shall we go to the park together after lunch?
You and I are late, so we must hurry.

meanings.definition: Working, because the power has been turned on.

examples.text: Please leave the light on when you go out.
Is the TV on? I can hear music.

meanings.definition: Onto or covering your body, used about clothes.

examples.text: Put your coat on because it is cold outside.
She had a red hat on at the party.

meanings.definition: Going forward or continuing without stopping.

examples.text: Go on, tell me what happened next.
He did not stop and walked on to the station.

meanings.definition: Touching and held up by the top of something.

examples.text: Your keys are on the kitchen table.
The cat is sleeping on my bed again.

meanings.definition: Used before a day or date to say when something happens.

examples.text: My birthday is on Friday this year.
We do not have school on Sunday.

meanings.definition: Inside a bus, train, plane or ship.

examples.text: I met my old friend on the bus today.
There were many people on the train this morning.

meanings.definition: Using or shown by a phone, TV, radio or computer.

examples.text: I watched a great film on TV last night.
She is talking to her mother on the phone.

meanings.definition: Used to say what a book, talk or piece of writing is about.

examples.text: She wrote a long book on the history of China.
The teacher gave a short talk on healthy food.

meanings.definition: In the company of someone or something.

examples.text: I go to school with my best friend.
Do you want to come with us to the park?

meanings.definition: Having or carrying something as a part or feature.

examples.text: She is the girl with the long black hair.
I want a house with a big garden.

meanings.definition: Using something to do an action.

examples.text: Please cut the bread with this knife.
He writes with a pen, not a pencil.

meanings.definition: Because of a feeling or condition that shows in your body.

examples.text: The little boy was shaking with cold.
Her face went red with anger.

meanings.definition: The person or thing near the speaker, which you point to or hold.

examples.text: Is this your pen on the floor?
This bag is too heavy for me.

meanings.definition: The day, week, year or part of a day that is happening now.

examples.text: I am very busy this week at work.
Did you eat breakfast this morning?

meanings.definition: Used when you tell people the name of someone next to you.

examples.text: Everyone, this is Maria, our new teacher.
Mum, this is my new friend from school.

meanings.definition: The person who is speaking or writing, when that person does the action.

examples.text: I am hungry, so can we eat now?
I live in a small house near the sea.

meanings.definition: In the same way that someone says or does something.

examples.text: As I told you, the meeting starts at nine.
Please do everything exactly as your teacher says.

meanings.definition: At the same moment that something else happens.

She smiled as she walked into the room.

meanings.definition: For the reason that.

examples.text: As it was raining, we stayed at home all day.
We took a taxi, as we were very late.

meanings.definition: Used to say what job or role someone has.

examples.text: My mother works as a nurse at the hospital.
He got a job as a cook in a hotel.

meanings.definition: At the time in your life when you were a certain kind of person.

examples.text: As a child, I lived in a small village.
She was very shy as a young girl.

meanings.definition: Used to say where someone or something is.

examples.text: My sister is at home with a cold.
We had lunch at a small restaurant today.

meanings.definition: Used to say the exact time when something happens.

examples.text: The film starts at eight o'clock tonight.
I get up at six every morning.

examples.text: The baby smiled at her mother.
Why are you looking at me like that?

meanings.definition: A woman or girl who has already been mentioned, when she does the action.

examples.text: My sister is a doctor, and she lives in London.
Where is Anna? She is not in class today.

meanings.definition: Used to join two ideas that are different or surprising together.

examples.text: I like tea, but my brother likes coffee.
The food was good but very expensive.

meanings.definition: Used after "not" to give the correct thing in place of the wrong one.

examples.text: The party is not on Friday but on Saturday.
She is not my sister but my cousin.

meanings.definition: Not including; apart from.

All the shops were closed but one.

meanings.definition: Used to show the place where someone or something starts or comes from.

She walked home from school in the rain.

meanings.definition: Used to show the time when something starts.

I work from Monday to Friday every week.

This birthday card is from all of us.

meanings.definition: Used to show what something is made out of.

Good butter is made from fresh cream.

meanings.definition: Used to say what kind of transport someone travels in.

examples.text: We go to school by bus every day.

examples.text: Her strong will to win helped her finish the race.
After the accident, his will to live kept him going.

examples.text: My grandfather left his house to me in his will.
She wrote a will so her children would get her money.

meanings.definition: What a person wants or chooses to do.

examples.text: They made him sign the paper against his will.
Nobody should be forced to marry against their will.

meanings.definition: Used between two or more things to show a choice.

examples.text: Do you want tea or coffee with your breakfast?
We can go by bus or by train tomorrow.

meanings.definition: Used to say what will happen if something is not done.

examples.text: Hurry up, or we will miss the last bus.
Wear a warm coat, or you will get cold outside.

examples.text: I don't eat meat or fish at all.
He never calls or writes to his parents.

examples.text: Workers want more say in how the company is run.
Children should have a say in where the family lives.

meanings.definition: To speak words to someone.

examples.text: The sign on the door says that the shop is closed.
What does the letter from the bank say?

My phone said the temperature outside was five degrees.

The milk will go bad if you leave it out.

The test was so hard that nobody finished it.

Tom was tired, and so was everyone else.

examples.text: So, what did you do at the weekend?
So, how was your first day at work?

I was hungry, so I made a sandwich.

meanings.definition: Used in "how about" or "what about" to suggest something.

I need a gift for Mum. What about some flowers?

Clothes and books were lying about the room.

meanings.definition: Used in questions to ask about one or more things from a group.

examples.text: Which color do you like best, red or blue?
There are two buses. Which goes to the station?

examples.text: The book which I bought yesterday is really good.
We stayed at a hotel which was near the beach.

examples.text: He passed the exam, which surprised everyone in the class.
She arrived late again, which made her boss angry.

meanings.definition: In or at a place that is not here.

She knows the area, so she can show us around.

examples.text: You should exercise more if you want to feel better.

They don't sell that kind of phone any more.

Can I have more bread with my soup, please?

examples.text: She earns more than her older brother.
There are more students in this class than in mine.

meanings.definition: To start to be in a new state.

examples.text: When does the next train leave for London?

This factory makes parts for cars and trucks.

What time does the next train leave?

meanings.definition: The thing or things that.

meanings.definition: From a lower part to a higher part of something.

examples.text: We walked up the hill to the old church.

meanings.definition: Along a road, river or path.

examples.text: Go up the road and turn left at the bank.

meanings.definition: The second one of two, or the ones that are left.

meanings.definition: Not at home or not at your place of work.

meanings.definition: From inside a place to the outside.

meanings.definition: Not giving light or heat any more.

examples.text: The fire went out during the cold night.

meanings.definition: In the same way that someone says or does something.

examples.text: As I told you, the meeting starts at nine.
Please do everything exactly as your teacher says.

meanings.definition: Used to say what job, role or purpose someone or something has.

examples.text: My mother works as a nurse at the hospital.
She uses her phone as an alarm clock every morning.

meanings.definition: Shows where someone or something comes from, or where a movement or period starts.

examples.text: Where are you from? I'm from Seoul.
She walked home from school in the rain.

meanings.definition: Used to show who sent or gave something.

examples.text: I got a nice letter from my grandmother.
This birthday card is from all of us.

meanings.definition: Used to show how far away one place is from another.

examples.text: The station is two kilometres from here.
We live far from the city centre.

meanings.definition: The time when it is one person's chance to play.

examples.text: It's your go now, so throw the dice.
Wait, it isn't your go yet. It's mine!

meanings.definition: Every person or thing in a group.

examples.text: All my friends came to my birthday party.
All the students in my class passed the test.

meanings.definition: The whole of a period of time, such as a day or night.

examples.text: It rained all day, so we stayed inside.
We worked in the garden all morning.

meanings.definition: The only thing, used to say that nothing more is needed.

examples.text: All I want right now is a hot shower.
All you need for this game is a pen.

meanings.definition: Towards a higher place or position.

examples.text: The bird flew up into the sky.
Everyone stood up when the teacher came in.

meanings.definition: Not in bed and not sleeping.

examples.text: Are you still up? It's very late.
The baby was up all night crying.

meanings.definition: One time that a scene of a film is filmed.

examples.text: The actor got the scene right on the first take.
The director needed ten takes for this short scene.

meanings.definition: A particular way of thinking about or understanding something.

examples.text: What's your take on the new plan for our school?
Her take on the film was very different from mine.
